title: Overhaul minor engine system components on agricultural equipment

lessons.title: Engine systems and preparing for the job
lessons.html:
Minor engine components

Tractors, combines, pumps and generators on farms mostly use diesel engines; small equipment like brush cutters, chainsaws and some pumps use petrol engines. A minor overhaul means removing, inspecting, cleaning, repairing or replacing components of an engine system without stripping the main engine. Examples include:

  • Fuel system: fuel filters, water separator, lift pump, fuel lines, bleeding the system
  • Air intake system: air cleaner elements, pre-cleaner, intake hoses and clamps
  • Cooling system: radiator, hoses, thermostat, water pump belt, fan, coolant
  • Lubrication system: oil filter, oil, breather, oil pressure sender
  • Electrical starting and charging: battery, starter motor connections, alternator belt
  • Exhaust system: manifold gaskets, silencer, clamps

Preparing for the job

  1. Read the job card and the operator's or workshop manual for the correct make and model.
  2. Get the correct parts, gaskets, filters and fluids, checking part numbers.
  3. Gather tools, including a torque wrench and drip trays.
  4. Park on level ground, lower implements, apply the park brake and chock wheels.
  5. Switch off the engine, remove the key and put a 'Do not operate' tag on the steering wheel.
  6. Let the engine cool before working on cooling or exhaust systems. Never open a hot radiator cap; hot coolant under pressure can cause severe burns.
  7. Disconnect the battery negative terminal before working on electrical components.

PPE

  • Safety glasses
  • Nitrile gloves for oil, fuel and coolant
  • Overalls and safety boots

Fire and environmental safety

Diesel and petrol are flammable. No smoking or open flames. Catch fluids in drip trays and clean spills immediately. Store used oil, coolant and filters for collection by an approved recycler.

lessons.title: Removing, inspecting and replacing components
lessons.html:
Working method

Removal

  • Clean around the component before removal so dirt does not enter the engine.
  • Label hoses and wires, or take photos on your phone, so they go back in the right place.
  • Cap or plug open fuel lines, oil ports and intake openings immediately.
  • Keep bolts and small parts in a labelled container.

Inspection

ComponentWhat to look for
HosesCracks, swelling, softness, hardening, leaks at clamps
BeltsCracks, glazing, fraying, correct tension
Air cleanerDirt load, damaged seals, cracked housing, loose clamps letting dust bypass
RadiatorBlocked fins with chaff or dirt, leaks, damaged cap seal
ThermostatOpens correctly when tested in hot water as per manual
Fuel linesLeaks, chafing, kinks
GasketsAlways replace; do not reuse old gaskets

Use measuring tools where the manual gives limits, such as belt deflection.

Replacing filters (example: diesel fuel filter)

  1. Close the fuel tap if fitted.
  2. Place a drip tray underneath.
  3. Remove the old filter and its sealing ring.
  4. Clean the filter head.
  5. Fit the new filter with a new seal, lightly oiled or wetted with clean fuel as the manual says. Tighten by hand to the specification; do not over-tighten.
  6. Bleed air from the fuel system following the manual: usually loosen bleed screws in order and operate the hand primer pump until fuel flows without bubbles.

Air in a diesel fuel system will stop the engine or cause hard starting, so bleeding is essential.

Cooling system

When replacing hoses or a thermostat, drain coolant into a clean container, fit new parts with new gaskets, refill with the coolant type and mix the manual specifies, and bleed air as instructed. Coolant is poisonous; keep it away from children and animals.

Belts

Release the tensioner, fit the new belt on all pulleys, and set the tension to the manual's specification. A loose belt slips and overheats; a tight belt damages bearings.

lessons.title: Reassembly, testing and recording
lessons.html:
Putting it back together

  • Fit components in the reverse order of removal, using your labels and photos.
  • Use new gaskets, seals and O-rings.
  • Tighten bolts to the torque specified in the manual, in the correct sequence where one is given.
  • Route hoses and wires as they were, with clamps, away from hot exhausts and moving parts.
  • Check that no tools, rags or loose parts are left in the engine bay.
  • Refill fluids to the correct level with the correct grade and type.
  • Reconnect the battery.

Testing

  1. Remove the tag only when you are ready, and make sure everyone is clear of the machine.
  2. Check fluid levels again before starting.
  3. Start the engine and watch the warning lights. The oil pressure light should go out within a few seconds. If it does not, stop the engine immediately.
  4. Let the engine idle and check for leaks of fuel, oil, coolant, air and exhaust.
  5. Check that belts run true and do not squeal.
  6. Run to operating temperature and check that the temperature gauge is normal and the thermostat opens (upper radiator hose gets hot).
  7. Stop the engine, let it settle, and recheck fluid levels. Top up as needed.
  8. Recheck hose clamps and fittings once cool.

Fault signs after repair

  • Hard starting or stalling: air in fuel system, blocked filter
  • Overheating: air lock in cooling system, wrong thermostat, loose belt
  • Black smoke: blocked air cleaner or intake restriction
  • Leaks: loose fittings, damaged or missing seals

Recording

Complete the job card: machine and hour meter reading, work done, parts and fluids used with quantities, test results, time spent and your signature. Update the service record so the next service is planned. Report any other problems you noticed.

Key points

  • Use the manual for the correct make and model, and the correct parts and fluids.
  • Park safely, tag the machine, let it cool and disconnect the battery.
  • Never open a hot radiator cap.
  • Clean before removal and cap open lines to keep dirt out.
  • Always fit new gaskets and seals and torque to specification.
  • Bleed fuel and cooling systems, test for leaks and record the work.
